title: Topic models for decision-support systems. Part I: Training, representation and exploitation of topic models
summary: This paper presents tase, a platform for expert-guided topic modeling combining Bayesian and Neural models with an innovative Solr-based exploitation framework for decision-support systems. It introduces scalable indexing, semantic similarity tools, and two real-world STI use cases.

title: ProxAnn: Use-Oriented Evaluations of Topic Models and Document Clustering
summary: This paper proposes a scalable human evaluation protocol and automated approximation for judging topic models and clustering systems under real-world user behavior. LLM proxies achieve performance comparable to human annotators.

title: Large Language Models Struggle to Describe the Haystack without Human Help: A Social Science-Inspired Evaluation of Large Research Language Models
summary: This study evaluates how users learn from LLM-based topic models versus traditional models. LLM-generated topics are readable but often overly generic; human supervision alleviates hallucination. Traditional LDA remains effective despite being less user-friendly.

title: Topic models for decision-support systems, Part II: Expert-in-the-loop hierarchical topic models
summary: This work introduces WS and DS, two expert-in-the-loop hierarchical topic modeling algorithms enabling domain experts to refine topic structures. The methods simplify tuning and integrate into IntelComp’s toolkit, showing strong performance across scientific datasets.

title: CASE: Large Scale Topic Exploitation for Decision Support Systems
summary: CASE introduces a Solr-based architecture for exploiting topic models at scale, enabling semantic search, topic inference, and STI indicator generation. Demonstrated through two real-world policy-support scenarios.

title: Discrepancy Detection at the Data Level: Toward Consistent Multilingual Question Answering
summary: MIND introduces a user-in-the-loop fact-checking pipeline for detecting factual and cultural inconsistencies in multilingual QA systems. Evaluated across datasets and domains, it identifies culturally-dependent divergences in QA responses.

title: ITMT: Interactive Topic Model Trainer
summary: ITMT is a GUI-driven tool enabling domain experts to train and refine topic models interactively, integrating classical and neural topic modeling libraries. The tool simplifies optimization and comparison across models.
